items.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Interviewer mentions George Martin in the context of Paul McCartney's 'Penny Lane' trumpet solo; Interviewee responds 'Right.' without adding personal interaction details.

ctx.x: is a wonderful ukulele player in Hawaii and we did a whole album with her, some jazz tunes, some folky, folkish kind of tunes, even one classical tune. We did the Faure “Pavane” kind of in the style of a Bill Evans with a symphony orchestra record. And except for her playing and a couple of jazz soloists that I got on the record, Arturo Sandoval, Ray Parker and Michael McDonald did a whole bunch of vocals on one of his tunes. But the rest was all me: drums and bass and keyboards and strings and everything, and…

Let me just wrap up, I forgot to ask about Paul McCartney, who over the years definitely knew what he wanted. I think of the “Penny Lane” trumpet solo and apparently how he vocalized it and had George Martin write it down.
